The SJC sustained the complaint in part (22-0-0), finding that Presbytery erred in…

artifacts.title: BCO 40-5 Matter re NW Georgia
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC, pursuant to citation by the 50th General Assembly under BCO 40-5, found that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred egregiously in approving calls and installing three candidates as associate pastors through a constitutionally deficient election process (slate voting, standing vote, failure to record number of voters present). The SJC stayed all further proceedings and declined to annul the installations, finding no PCA precedent for such relief.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Michael Woodham complained that South Florida Presbytery erred by excommunicating a Teaching Elder it had previously deposed without first assigning him to membership in a particular church as required by BCO 46-8. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that Presbytery retained jurisdiction over a deposed minister until transfer to a local church was completed, and that Presbytery's efforts to implement BCO 46-8 showed no clear error; two concurring opinions (RE Donahoe and RE Eggert) offered alternative reasoning regarding the scope of Presbytery's residual jurisdiction.

artifacts.title: Doty v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Ms. Doty and 21 others filed charges against a Nashville Presbytery teaching elder first with his congregation's Session (wrong court), then with Nashville Presbytery; Presbytery declined to indict and treated the matter as a report under BCO 31-2 rather than charges. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order (11-9-2-2) on the ground that Doty lacked standing under BCO 43-1 as a non-member of Nashville Presbytery; a significant dissent argued that her filing of charges gave her standing under prior precedent (Lyons, Ruff, Fordice).

artifacts.title: Sawyers et al. v. Missouri Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Complainants alleged Missouri Presbytery erred in failing to find a strong presumption of guilt that TE Jeffrey Meyers held views contrary to the Westminster Standards in its BCO 31-2 investigation. The SJC found that MOP erred but declared the case moot because MOP had already conducted a trial of TE Meyers during the pendency of the case before the SJC.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in finding no strong presumption of guilt in TE Joshua Moon after an investigation into allegations that his theological views on Federal Vision topics were heterodox, holding that deference to the presbytery was required absent clear error in the record. The case generated a concurring opinion offering procedural guidance on BCO 31-2 investigations versus BCO 32-2 charges, and a dissenting opinion by RE Haigler arguing the record showed unambiguous heterodoxy warranting a finding of strong presumption of guilt.

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Peter B. Kim appealed his deposition and excommunication by Korean Eastern Presbytery on charges of contumacy and threatening members with civil litigation. The SJC sustained the contumacy charge and deposition but reduced the excommunication to indefinite suspension from the sacraments as excessive; it declined to rule on the civil-threat charge because the relevant letter was not in the Record of the Case.

artifacts.title: Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery (Complaint)
artifacts.synopsis: TE Peter B. Kim complained that Korean Eastern Presbytery erred in denying his complaint regarding unconstitutional actions of KEP's Administrative Commission, which had unlawfully exercised judicial powers in ordering a congregational meeting and dissolving his pastoral relationship. The SJC agreed KEP erred but held the matter moot in light of Kim's deposition in Case 2005-8, with a dissent arguing the constitutional violations by KEP were serious and should have been remedied.

artifacts.title: Smith v. Southwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Beverly R. Smith appealed her conviction on four charges (factiousness, gossip/slander, breaking membership vows, and contumacy) by the session of Covenant Presbyterian Church, which was upheld by Southwest Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, finding the documentary evidence insufficient to prove the charges and that the session committed multiple procedural errors including failure to produce witnesses, prejudice, and improper suspension from the sacraments before charges were disclosed.

artifacts.title: Nickoley v. Rocky Mountain
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC found that Rocky Mountain Presbytery erred in immediately deposing Rev. Bruce Nickoley from ministry on a contumacy charge without providing him due process rights and a full trial. The case was remanded for either proper trial or revocation of the deposition judgment.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Stuart Merriam, a minister transferred from PCUSA to Tennessee Valley Presbytery in 1986, was subject to ecclesiastical discipline based on his criminal conviction in Papua New Guinea. The SJC sustained Merriam's appeal, finding that TVP violated due process principles and procedures under the BCO, particularly by failing to appoint counsel and conducting an inadequate trial. The case was remanded to TVP for a new trial following proper BCO procedures.

artifacts.title: Steve Newton vs. Heartland Presbytery & Grace RPC Session vs. Heartland Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace Reformed Presbyterian Church appealed its conviction for contumacy and termination of its relationship with Heartland Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, holding that a presbytery lacks original jurisdiction to indict and try a session (lower court) for an offense such as contumacy, as BCO provisions reserve original jurisdiction over ruling elders to the Session level.
